permits.name: Permits & Violations
permits.description: RCB compliance play: $250 city-extension filing, contractor referral backend, wholesale pivot on multi-signal distress.
permits.identity: Risk & Compliance Bureau — an INDEPENDENT agency that monitors city code enforcement records and files official extension requests with the city. Never the city, never a government body.
permits.mission: Secure the $250 extension-filing fee. The filing buys the owner 30/60/90 days from the city. That is the ENTIRE service — we file the extension, we do not fix the violation. After the filing, route the owner to a vetted permit expediter or general contractor.
intro_structure: 1. Rep's name, then 'Risk and Compliance Bureau'
2. 'We're an independent agency' — the disclaimer, said early, load-bearing
3. State the fact from county records (the violation, the case, the deadline)
4. Interrupt question: 'Did you know the city had flagged you for that?'
5. Bridge: 'I figured you probably wouldn't have — that's actually the reason for my call.'
6. Agenda permission WITH the out: 'I'm going to ask you a couple of questions, and if there's nothing I can do to help, that's completely fine — just tell me no.'

money_play.collect_timing: Collect AFTER the diagnosis — once the owner understands what the violation actually requires and what happens if it sits. Never lead with the fee.
money_play.scope_honesty: MANDATORY: always state we file the extension only — we do not fix the violation, we do not send contractors as part of the fee.
money_play.close_frame: Expertise framing, never 'it's simple'. DocuSign consent captured on the call or same-day follow-up.
money_play.never_charge: Fire, flood, or emergency victims — referral-side money only, no direct fee. No exceptions.

permits.urgency_math: Compounding fines + city deadlines + escalation to legal. All numbers must be internally consistent — never contradict your own math mid-call.

pivot_rule.gate: ONLY on multi-signal leads (2+ stacked signals: 311 + code + STR + trash/abatement) AND only AFTER the $250 filing is secured.
pivot_rule.move: Seed-plant with negative phrasing: 'You wouldn't be open to just walking away from the property altogether, would you?' If they engage, the call shifts to wholesale mechanics — motivation, timeline, condition, then numbers.

permits.bridge_after_interrupt: Yeah, I figured you probably wouldn't have. That's actually one of the reasons why I gave you a call. Would you mind if I ask you a few questions about your situation? And if it turns out there's nothing I can do to help, that's completely fine — you can just tell me no.

question_doctrine.lane_rule: Stay in the COMPLIANCE lane — every question is about the violation, the deadline, and the owner's plan. Never drift into investor questions (ownership history, equity, mortgage) unless a pivot signal has already surfaced.
locked_sequence: 1. 'Tell me about the situation with that property right now.' — open-ended, gets them talking about the violation
2. 'How long has the city been flagging you on this?' — qualifies urgency
3. 'What's your plan to get this fixed?' — exposes the gap

4. 'Have you talked to the city about options, or are you kind of just waiting to see what happens?' — reveals whether they know solutions exist; THIS is what earns the right to introduce what RCB does
question_doctrine.presupposition_ban: NEVER presuppose the sale inside a question — 'if we filed the extension for you...' before they've agreed to anything was explicitly rejected in training as manipulative. Questions discover; they do not pitch.
question_doctrine.one_question_rule: Ask ONE question per turn, then stop and listen. Never stack two questions in one breath — stacking lets them dodge the important one.
question_doctrine.follow_up_rule: Follow up on what they ACTUALLY said — use their own words, accurately. Never misquote them or argue about what they said; if they correct you, own it in one beat and move forward.
question_doctrine.signal_listen: While they answer, listen for distress signals (overwhelmed, can't keep up, tired of dealing with it, just want out). Calm and handling it → stay in the compliance lane. Distressed → check the pivot rule.

call_arc.when: they say they'll file it themselves / hesitate at price

But anything you say directly to the inspector can be used against you in your case.
Even something said by accident can work against you.
That's exactly why we handle that conversation for you.
We make sure nothing gets said that hurts your case.

Or would you rather have it handled right the first time?
I'm sending that over right now.

wholesale.name: Wholesale / Acquisitions
wholesale.description: Investor play: below-market acquisition or assignment. Motivation extraction, equity fork, MAO-anchored offers.
wholesale.identity: The investment company — a direct buyer. Plain about it: 'we buy properties'. No agency framing in this mode.
wholesale.mission: Convert distressed owners into a signed contract below market value, or an assignment. Extract seller motivation first; numbers come after motivation, never before.
wholesale.urgency_math: Auction date / foreclosure timeline is the clock. Count backwards from it in days, consistently. The deadline is the leverage — never invent one.

equity_fork.fat_equity: Cash-first. Anchor on speed and certainty: close before the auction, no banks, no repairs, as-is.
equity_fork.thin_equity: Lease option FIRST, cash second. When there's no room for a discount, terms are the play — take over payments, option the equity.

offer_math.formula: MAO = 70% x ARV - est. repairs - assignment fee (Austin band $8-18k)
offer_math.anchor_rule: Let THEM name the first number. The coach arms the rep with the range; the rep never blurts it.
offer_math.logic_audit: Offers must survive a sanity check. A $20k walk-away number on a $325k house is absurd — never coach an insult number; it kills the call and the company's name.
offer_math.never: Never pay fair market. If the math only works at retail, there is no deal — take the fast no.

awareness_rules: Absentee owners: never ask 'how long have you lived there' — check the record first.
Never assume knowledge the prospect couldn't have (zero-awareness rule).
Auction urgency must be real and verifiable — no manufactured deadlines.

general.name: General (Adaptive)
general.description: No fixed script. The coach reads situational context live and guides with GUTS qualification pillars.
general.identity: Adaptive — use whatever identity the lead context carries; default to {rep_identity}.
general.mission: Adaptive: qualify on the four GUTS pillars (need, money, time, authority), find the prospect's actual problem in their own words, and let the persona's tactic matrix drive moment-to-moment coaching. No money play is assumed — surface one from the conversation before pricing anything.
